title: Four-unit zoning for low-density neighbourhoods
subtitle: Development approval funding, emergency plan, Canadian Tire expansion, community space plan and a veterans memorial banner program
overview: Council directed staff to prepare a zoning change allowing up to four residential units and four storeys as of right in low-density residential zones, with a report due in the first quarter of 2024. The motion also reaffirmed the city's Affordable Housing Strategy and its pledge of 16,000 new homes by 2031, and will be sent to the federal housing minister as part of the city's Housing Accelerator Fund application {{vote:m7}}.

Council also approved the Streamline Development Approval Fund report, including one new Assistant City Solicitor position to be funded from 2023 staff savings {{vote:m3}}. It approved an updated Emergency Response Plan and a new Emergency Management Program By-law {{vote:m5}}, and a zoning change allowing Canadian Tire to expand its Erb Street West store {{vote:m6}}.

Council accepted a status update on the Indoor Community Space Master Plan {{vote:m4}} and asked staff to report on a memorial banner program for veterans {{vote:m8}}. Together these affect how much housing can be built in existing neighbourhoods, how the city prepares for emergencies, and what recreation and arts space is planned. Council also held a closed meeting on labour relations and council orientation; the minutes report no decisions from it.

decisions.item: Four units and four storeys as of right
decisions.detail: Staff will start a Zoning By-law 2018-050 amendment to permit up to four units and four storeys in low-density residential zones, report back in Q1 2024, and review intensification and missing middle housing through the Official Plan Review.
Council approved the report, the hiring of an Assistant City Solicitor funded from 2023 staff savings with ongoing funding referred to the 2024-2026 operating budget, and a thank-you to the Province.
Council approved the updated Emergency Response Plan and the Emergency Management Program By-law.

decisions.item: Canadian Tire zoning amendment, Erb Street West
decisions.detail: Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-09 for 650, 654, 656 and 660 Erb St W, enabling the store expansion.
Council accepted the report as a status update on the 10-year plan.
Staff will report back on the possibility of a memorial banner program, raised in connection with honouring veterans.

debate: On the housing motion, delegates supported it but urged more: eliminating parking minimums, relaxing setbacks and height limits, and regulating short-term rentals. One delegate worried that the wording on appropriate zoning regulations could let opponents block housing.

Councillors supporting the housing motion said it adds one more tool for housing supply, and that uptake may be modest because of renovation costs. Others raised tree canopy protection, drainage, paving over backyards, traffic on cul-de-sacs, and servicing capacity. Staff said the motion gives enough flexibility and that the nodes and corridors approach continues.

On the Canadian Tire expansion, councillors raised pedestrian safety in and around the plaza, crime prevention at the rear fence, and noise from deliveries, noting limited by-law tools. The applicant's representative said deliveries are not overnight and that a noise study and peer review recommended no mitigation. Councillors also asked about future housing on the site; the applicant said none is planned now.

On the Streamline fund report, councillors asked how parking reductions fit with the planning study findings and how Council will weigh in during the Official Plan Review. Staff said parking rates are being refined and the plan will be brought forward in smaller topic-based pieces.

On the emergency plan, councillors asked about backup alerting, scenario planning and training. Staff said door-to-door notice is the fallback and recommended a dedicated emergency management position. Councillors asked that Council understand the acting mayor's role, and orientation training was scheduled for the following week.
